fact: MACRA says the World Bank-supported Digital Malawi Acceleration Project is procuring service providers to roll out more than 90 new towers to address connectivity gaps in underserved and rural areas, with USF budget funds continuing for further expansion.

Ecofin Agency reports that under the World Bank-funded DMAP the government is preparing to deploy 100 towers in underserved and rural areas, with the Universal Service Fund and procurement being prepared, and that MACRA will keep using USF resources for further sites.
Nyasa Times reports DMAP project manager Chimwemwe Matemba saying a plan to deploy 100 mobile phone towers in underserved areas, with the Universal Service Fund, has entered procurement preparation.
Tech Africa News reports the government has switched on the 36th rural telecommunications tower under the Last Mile Rural Connectivity Project, at Kalira Village, covering about 10 square kilometres.
Tech Africa News reports the government plans 99 further towers under the rural connectivity programme, targeted for completion by June 2027.
Macra's USF head Ronald Tembo said Macra is working on a data corridor and on introducing data to cover all rural areas with affordable and reliable internet.
Under DMAP, safeguards assessments are complete for over 500 public institutions earmarked for connectivity and 100 telecom towers planned for rural and underserved communities.
